title_en: Weng Like v. Shanghai Pudong Yiwei Fuel Injection Co., Ltd. and Shanghai Diesel Engine Co., Ltd. — dispute over remuneration for service invention designer
ruling_gist_en: According to Article 16 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 76 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, where a state-owned enterprise or institution that has been granted a patent right licenses others to exploit its patent, it shall, after tax, extract no less than 10% from the royalties collected for licensing the patent as remuneration to be paid to the inventor or designer. According to Article 47(2) of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, a decision declaring a patent right invalid shall have no retroactive effect on any judgment or order on patent infringement that has been rendered and enforced by the people's court before the declaration of invalidation, on any decision on the handling of a patent infringement dispute that has been performed or compulsorily enforced before the declaration of invalidation, or on any contract for patent exploitation licensing and any contract for patent assignment that have been performed before the declaration of invalidation. However, compensation shall be made for any loss caused to others by the patentee's malicious intent. According to the above provisions, in a case where an inventor or designer brings a lawsuit requesting the patentee who has licensed others to exploit the patent to pay remuneration for a service invention-creator in accordance with the law, even if the patent is declared invalid due to lack of novelty, and the patentee refuses to pay the remuneration for a service invention-creator that should have been paid for the patent exploitation licensing acts that occurred before the declaration of invalidity on the ground that the patent has been declared invalid, the people's court shall still not support such refusal.

full_text_en:
Weng Like v. Shanghai Pudong Yiwei Fuel Injection Co., Ltd. and Shanghai Diesel Engine Co., Ltd. — dispute over remuneration for service invention designer

【Ruling Summary】

Pursuant to Article 16 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 76 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, where a state-owned enterprise or institution that has been granted a patent right licenses others to exploit its patent, it shall, after tax, extract no less than 10% from the royalties collected for licensing the exploitation of the patent as remuneration to be paid to the inventor or designer. Pursuant to Article 47, Paragraph 2 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, a decision declaring a patent right invalid shall have no retroactive effect on any judgment or order on patent infringement that has been rendered and enforced by a people's court prior to the declaration of invalidity, on any decision on patent infringement dispute that has been performed or compulsorily executed, or on any patent exploitation license contract and patent assignment contract that have been performed prior to the declaration of invalidity; however, compensation shall be made for any loss caused to another person as a result of the patentee's bad faith. According to the above provisions, in a case where an inventor or designer files a lawsuit claiming that a patentee who has licensed others to exploit the patent should pay remuneration for the service invention designer in accordance with the law, even if the patent is declared invalid due to lack of novelty, the patentee, on the ground that the patent has been declared invalid, refuses to pay the remuneration for the service invention designer that has already accrued from the patent exploitation license conducted prior to the declaration of invalidity, the people's court shall not support such refusal.

Plaintiff: Weng Like, male, Han ethnicity, 65 years old, residing at Baihua Road, Shanghai.

Defendant: Shanghai Pudong Yiwei Fuel Injection Co., Ltd., domiciled at Pudong Avenue, Shanghai.
Legal Representative: Bai Hongfa, Chairman of the Company.

Defendant: Shanghai Diesel Engine Co., Ltd., domiciled at Pudong Avenue, Shanghai.
Legal Representative: Chen Longxing, Chairman of the Company.

The plaintiff, Weng Like, filed a lawsuit with the Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court against the defendants, Shanghai Pudong Yiwei Fuel Injection Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yiwei Company) and Shanghai Diesel Engine Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shangchai Company), concerning a dispute over remuneration for a service invention designer.

The plaintiff, Weng Like, alleged: The plaintiff previously served at the defendant Yiwei Company and was the first completer and main contributor of two scientific and technological achievements, namely the "P7N type fuel injection pump assembly" and the "PE type fuel injection pump assembly." Among the aforementioned scientific and technological achievements, the two technologies, namely the "locking spring device for the roller tappet of the fuel injection pump" and the "rectangular cross-section plunger spring fuel injection pump," were the plaintiff's service inventions. On April 17, 2001, the parent company of Yiwei Company, i.e., the defendant Shangchai Company, applied for the patents-in-suit with the State Intellectual Property Office of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the SIPO), and obtained the patent rights on January 23 of the following year. On November 1, 2003, Shangchai Company and Yiwei Company entered into a contract to transfer the patents-in-suit to Yiwei Company without consideration. On November 4, 2003, Yiwei Company and a third party, Shanghai Denso Fuel Injection Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Denso Company), signed the "P7 and PE Type Diesel Fuel Injection Pump Technology Transfer Agreement." According to this agreement, Denso Company was to pay Yiwei Company an initial fee of RMB 2.5 million and a technology royalty of 4% of the net selling price of the products. As of December 31, 2005, Denso Company had paid a technology royalty of over RMB 5.98 million for the "P7 type diesel fuel injection pump technology" and an initial fee of RMB 2.5 million as well as a royalty of over RMB 10.9 million for the "PE type diesel fuel injection pump technology." In addition, Yiwei Company had also manufactured and sold related products that used the patents-in-suit. Article 76 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law) provides: "Where a state-owned enterprise or institution that has been granted a patent right licenses any other entity or individual to exploit its patent, it shall, after tax, extract no less than 10% from the royalties collected for licensing the exploitation of the patent as remuneration to be paid to the inventor or designer." The "Several Opinions on Further Strengthening Intellectual Property Work in Shanghai" and the "Notice on Several Supporting Policies for Implementing the 'Shanghai Medium- and Long-Term Science and Technology Development Plan (2006-2020)'" both stipulate that a patentee may, after licensing others to exploit the patent, extract no less than 30% of the after-tax income as remuneration for the designer. The plaintiff was the first completer and main contributor of the scientific and technological achievements "P7N type fuel injection pump assembly" and "PE type fuel injection pump assembly" and was the sole inventor of the "locking spring device for the roller tappet of the fuel injection pump" and the "rectangular cross-section plunger spring fuel injection pump." Since Shangchai Company and Yiwei Company licensed others to exploit the patents, they should pay the plaintiff corresponding service remuneration in accordance with the law. In summary, the plaintiff requested the people's court to order the two defendants to pay the plaintiff RMB 2 million as service remuneration for the licensing fees of the two service invention patents accrued up to April 2007.

When filing the lawsuit, the plaintiff also claimed three other items, including service remuneration for the defendant Yiwei Company's self-exploitation of the patents. After changing the claims twice, the plaintiff withdrew those claims but reserved the right to pursue those service remuneration interests in a separate action.

The defendants Yiwei Company and Shangchai Company argued: 1. The plaintiff, Weng Like, has no right to claim service remuneration for the two patents-in-suit, namely the "P7N type fuel injection pump assembly" and the "PE type fuel injection pump assembly," from Yiwei Company. The two patents-in-suit were not completed during the plaintiff's tenure at the defendant Yiwei Company but were completed by relevant technical personnel of Shangchai Company in 1994. On November 1, 2003, Shangchai Company and Yiwei Company entered into a contract to transfer the patents-in-suit to Yiwei Company. Yiwei Company's licensing of the transferred patents to a third party naturally does not require the payment of remuneration to its own staff; 2. Weng Like has no right to claim service remuneration for the two patents-in-suit from Shangchai Company. Both patents-in-suit have been declared invalid. Shangchai Company did not obtain any benefit from the patent transfer, so there is no basis for paying service remuneration to the plaintiff; 3. The amount of service remuneration claimed by the plaintiff is unreasonable. The two service inventions owned by the plaintiff are merely components of the relevant fuel injection pump assembly, with the contribution of these inventions to the fuel injection pump assembly being only 3.65%. The plaintiff's claim for RMB 2 million has no legal basis. In summary, the plaintiff's claims lack factual and legal grounds and should not be supported.

The Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court found the following facts in the first instance:

The defendant Shangchai Company was one of the shareholders of the defendant Yiwei Company, holding 90% of Yiwei Company's registered capital. The plaintiff, Weng Like, served as the chief engineer of Yiwei Company from the date of its establishment on December 15, 1995, until his retirement in March 2005.

On April 17, 2001, the defendant Shangchai Company filed applications with the SIPO for utility model patents entitled "Locking Spring Device for Roller Tappet of Fuel Injection Pump" and "Rectangular Cross-Section Plunger Spring Fuel Injection Pump." On January 23, 2002, the SIPO decided to grant the two patent rights to Shangchai Company, with patent numbers ZL01238898.X and ZL01238896.3, and the designer listed on the patent certificates was the plaintiff, Weng Like.

In September 2003, the defendant Shangchai Company and the defendant Yiwei Company discussed and believed that since Yiwei Company was a subsidiary of Shangchai Company, patent applications were uniformly filed by Shangchai Company, and therefore the patentee was recorded as Shangchai Company at that time. As market economy awareness increased and issues concerning intellectual property ownership arose, the above three patents should belong to Yiwei Company, and legal procedures for the transfer of patent rights should be handled. Both parties reached a consensus and jointly signed a written explanation. On November 1 of the same year, Shangchai Company and Yiwei Company signed two "Patent Right Assignment Contracts," agreeing that Shangchai Company would transfer the patent rights of ZL01238898.X and ZL01238896.3 to Yiwei Company without consideration. The registration date for the transfer of the "Rectangular Cross-Section Plunger Spring Fuel Injection Pump" patent right was February 27, 2004, and for the "Locking Spring Device for Roller Tappet of Fuel Injection Pump" patent right, it was April 23, 2004.

On November 4, 2003, the defendant Yiwei Company, as the licensor, and the third party Denso Company, as the licensee, signed the "P7 and PE Type Diesel Fuel Injection Pump Technology Transfer Agreement," which provided: "...6.1: As consideration for the provision of technical information pursuant to Section 3.1 of this Agreement and the licensing rights granted under Section 2 of this Agreement, the Licensee shall pay the Licensor the following amounts: (1) an initial fee, which is non-refundable, of RMB zero (￥0000) for the P7 type diesel fuel injection pump (hereinafter referred to as the P7 pump) and RMB two million five hundred thousand (￥2,500,000) for the PE type diesel fuel injection pump (hereinafter referred to as the PE pump), payable by the Licensee to the Licensor in a single lump sum within sixty days after the effective date of this Agreement... (2) a technology royalty, which is non-refundable, equal to four percent (4%) of the net selling price of the contract products sold or otherwise disposed of by the Licensee during the term of this Agreement... 7.3: The Licensor shall pay taxes on its own in accordance with the tax collection provisions of the People's Republic of China..." The aforementioned agreement also included as attachments the "Technical Characteristics of P7 and PE Type Diesel Fuel Injection Pumps," "Patent List," and "Technical Information." After the agreement took effect, Yiwei Company received the initial fee of RMB 2.5 million as stipulated in the agreement. According to the summary of royalty receipts provided by Yiwei Company, the royalty amounts before deduction of various taxes (business tax, surcharges, corporate income tax) were: For the P7 pump, the royalty income for 2003, 2004, 2005, 2006, and January to April 2007 were RMB 303,227.66, RMB 4,000,821.22, RMB 1,678,563.97, RMB 2,267,125.80, and RMB 912,224.01 respectively; for the PE pump, the royalty income for 2003, 2004, 2005, 2006, and January to April 2007 were RMB 282,654.95, RMB 5,448,673.97, RMB 5,175,504.24, RMB 3,827,915.48, and RMB 1,383,375.81 respectively. Based on these amounts, Yiwei Company calculated that after deducting business tax, surcharges, and corporate income tax, the net income from the P7 pump royalty for 2003, 2004, 2005, 2006, and January to April 2007 were RMB 243,438.74, RMB 3,211,959.30, RMB 1,347,593.12, RMB 1,820,105.27, and RMB 732,356.24 respectively; the net income from the PE pump initial fee after deducting business tax, surcharges, and corporate income tax was RMB 2,007,062.50, and the net income from the PE pump royalty for 2003, 2004, 2005, 2006, and January to April 2007 after deducting business tax, surcharges, and corporate income tax were RMB 226,922.46, RMB 4,374,331.68, RMB 4,155,024.19, RMB 3,073,146.25, and RMB 1,110,608.68 respectively. The plaintiff, Weng Like, argued that the two defendants did not provide separate tax vouchers specifically for the licensing fees of the P7 pump and PE pump, but only general tax vouchers, and therefore questioned whether there were any tax exemptions or reductions related to the taxes and whether the taxes were actually paid. Yiwei Company stated that the taxes involved in the summary had been actually paid and there were no tax exemptions or reductions. Both the plaintiff and defendants acknowledged that the P7 pump assembly technology covered by the agreement contained one patent, namely the "Locking Spring Device for Roller Tappet of Fuel Injection Pump," and the PE pump assembly technology contained two patents, namely the "Locking Spring Device for Roller Tappet of Fuel Injection Pump" and the "Rectangular Cross-Section Plunger Spring Fuel Injection Pump."

On July 7, 2005, the Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Patent Reexamination Board) accepted the request for invalidation of the patent rights ZL01238898.X and ZL01238896.3 filed by the third party Denso Company on the same day. On December 23, 2005, based on the special value-added tax invoice issued by the defendant Yiwei Company to the defendant Shangchai Company on August 31, 1999, and the assembly detail sheet of Shangchai Company, the Patent Reexamination Board, on the ground that a product identical to the technical solution protected by the patent claims had been publicly sold before the patent application date and thus lacked novelty, issued a decision declaring both ZL01238898.X and ZL01238896.3 utility model patent rights completely invalid. Yiwei Company did not take any measures to respond to the invalidation of the patents. During the trial, Yiwei Company stated that due to a staff error, the complaint for an administrative lawsuit to be filed with the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court was mistakenly sent to the Patent Reexamination Board, causing a delay and resulting in the court refusing to accept the case on the ground that the lawsuit was not filed within the statute of limitations, and a return notice was issued.

The Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with the law, entrusted the Shanghai Science and Technology Consulting Service Center (hereinafter referred to as the STCSC) to conduct an appraisal on two issues: (1) the technical proportion of the patents-in-suit in the relevant fuel injection pump assembly (i.e., the quantification of the role of the patents-in-suit in the relevant fuel injection pump assembly from a technical perspective); and (2) the technical proportion of the P7 pump and PE pump assembly technologies in the "P7 and PE Type Diesel Fuel Injection Pump Technology Transfer Agreement" at issue. Regarding the first issue, the STCSC issued the "Technical Appraisal Report" (Shanghai Science and Technology Consulting Service Center [2006] Appraisal No. 027), which divided the overall technology of the fuel injection pump assembly into imported technology, collective independent development technology, and patented technology developed independently with intellectual property rights. The conclusion was: In the overall technology of the fuel injection pump assembly containing the "Locking Spring Device for Roller Tappet of Fuel Injection Pump" patent, the technical contribution rate of the imported technology was approximately 50%, the technical contribution rate of the collective independent development technology during the process of digesting and absorbing the imported technology was approximately 45%, and the technical contribution rate of the ZL01238898.X utility model patent was approximately 5%; in the overall technology of the fuel injection pump assembly containing the "Locking Spring Device for Roller Tappet of Fuel Injection Pump" and "Rectangular Cross-Section Plunger Spring Fuel Injection Pump" patents, the technical contribution rate of the imported technology was approximately 40%, the technical contribution rate of the collective independent development technology during the process of digesting and absorbing the imported technology was approximately 50%, and the technical contribution rate of the two utility model patents ZL01238898.X and ZL01238896.3 was approximately 10%. Regarding the second issue, the STCSC issued the "Supplementary Appraisal Report" (Shanghai Science and Technology Consulting Service Center [2006] Appraisal No. 027-1), which considered that the elements creating the value of the P7 pump and PE pump were mainly three aspects: technology (design and process), manufacturing, and management, while the assembly technology included two aspects: technology (design and process) and manufacturing. The two patents-in-suit fell within the scope of the design technology of the contract products under the agreement. Based on a specific analysis of the "Technical Information" attachment to the agreement, the supplementary appraisal concluded that the technical proportion of the P7 pump and PE pump assembly technologies in the entire transferred content under the agreement was approximately 70%, and the proportion of the management system in the entire transferred content under the agreement was approximately 30%.

During the trial, the defendants Shangchai Company and Yiwei Company provided the "Refund and Supplementary Agreement to the 'P7 and PE Type Diesel Fuel Injection Pump Technology Transfer Agreement'" and a credit voucher for Yiwei Company's refund to the third party Denso Company, claiming that Yiwei Company and Denso Company had negotiated and determined the proportion of the patents-in-suit in the transferred technology, and after the patents were declared invalid, Yiwei Company had refunded the licensing fees previously collected for the patents to Denso Company. Yiwei Company also provided receipts for the payment of the plaintiff's housing purchase funds and bonus awards, claiming that Yiwei Company had paid the plaintiff, Weng Like, a reward of over RMB 200,000, but the dates of the aforementioned receipts were before the "P7 and PE Type Diesel Fuel Injection Pump Technology Transfer Agreement."

The issues in dispute in this case at first instance were: 1. Whether the plaintiff, Weng Like, had the right to claim service remuneration for the two patents-in-suit, namely the "P7N type fuel injection pump assembly" and the "PE type fuel injection pump assembly," from the defendants Yiwei Company and Shangchai Company. 2. If the plaintiff had the right to claim, how should the calculation method for the remuneration be determined.

The Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court held in the first instance:

1. Regarding the first issue in dispute.

Article 16 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Patent Law) provides: "The entity that has been granted a patent right shall reward the inventor or designer of a service invention-creation; after the invention-creation patent is exploited, the inventor or designer shall be given a reasonable remuneration based on the extent of its dissemination and application and the economic benefits derived." Article 76 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law provides: "Where a state-owned enterprise or institution that has been granted a patent right licenses any other entity or individual to exploit its patent, it shall, after tax, extract no less than 10% from the royalties collected for licensing the exploitation of the patent as remuneration to be paid to the inventor or designer." The defendants Yiwei Company and Shangchai Company provided drawings of the plunger spring, tappet components, and the P7 reinforced pump, claiming that the patents-in-suit were completed by employees of Shangchai Company. However, on the one hand, the designer recorded on the patent certificates of the patents-in-suit was the plaintiff, Weng Like; on the other hand, when Shangchai Company transferred the patents-in-suit to Yiwei Company without consideration, the consensus reached between the parties was that the patents-in-suit should belong to Yiwei Company, and the patentee was recorded as Shangchai Company only because Yiwei Company was a subsidiary of Shangchai Company and patent applications were uniformly filed by Shangchai Company. This was confirmed by the written explanation jointly signed by both parties. Moreover, the drawings provided by the two defendants themselves could not serve as direct evidence that the patents-in-suit were completed by employees of Shangchai Company. Considering the above factors comprehensively, the court did not accept the two defendants' assertion that the plaintiff was not the designer of the utility model patents "Locking Spring Device for Roller Tappet of Fuel Injection Pump" and "Rectangular Cross-Section Plunger Spring Fuel Injection Pump." The plaintiff was entitled to claim reasonable remuneration for the two service inventions. Yiwei Company licensed the third party Denso Company to exploit the aforementioned patents and collected royalties; it should, in accordance with the law, extract a certain percentage from such royalties as remuneration to be paid to the plaintiff. As for the plaintiff's claim that Shangchai Company should bear joint and several liability for the payment of remuneration, the agreement for the licensing and exploitation of the patents-in-suit was signed by Yiwei Company, and Yiwei Company was the entity that obtained the benefits from such licensing. Shangchai Company's transfer of the patent rights to Yiwei Company was to resolve issues concerning intellectual property ownership, and Shangchai Company did not license others to use the patents. The plaintiff also acknowledged that the service inventions in question were completed during his tenure at Yiwei Company. Therefore, the court did not support the plaintiff's claim that Shangchai Company should bear joint and several liability.

**Translation of Part 2/2:**

At the trial, the Defendants Shangchai Company and Yiwei Company submitted the "Refund and Supplemental Agreement Regarding the 'P7 and PE Type Diesel Injection Pump Technology Transfer Agreement,'" asserting that Yiwei Company and Denso Corporation had already negotiated and confirmed the proportion of the disputed patents within the transferred technology, and that after the patents were declared invalid, the license fees previously collected for the patents were refunded to Denso Corporation. First, the proportion of the patents-in-suit within the transferred technology is an important fact to be determined in this case, which is relevant to determining the amount of remuneration claimed by Plaintiff Weng Like and also contradicts the expert appraisal issued by the Science and Technology Consulting Center. The content of the supplemental agreement entered into by the two defendants and Denso Corporation is not binding upon the plaintiff, who is a third party to the supplemental agreement, nor can it be directly used as a basis for determining the facts of this case. The proportion of the patents-in-suit within the transferred technology should be based on the expert appraisal issued by the Science and Technology Consulting Center. Second, Article 47(2) of the Patent Law provides: "The decision declaring a patent right invalid shall have no retroactive effect on any judgment or order on patent infringement that has been rendered and enforced by the people's court before the declaration of invalidity, on any decision concerning the handling of patent infringement disputes that has been performed or compulsorily enforced, or on any patent exploitation license contract and patent assignment contract that have been performed prior to the declaration of invalidity. However, compensation shall be made for any loss caused to others by the patentee's malice." Therefore, before the patent-in-suit in this case was declared invalid, the patent exploitation licensing acts that had already occurred between Defendant Yiwei Company and Denso Corporation are valid. Yiwei Company is still required to pay remuneration to the creator of the service invention-creation in accordance with relevant laws and regulations. Furthermore, Yiwei Company argued that it had already rewarded the plaintiff and submitted relevant documents. Regarding this issue, on the one hand, these rewards given by Yiwei Company to the plaintiff do not constitute payment of remuneration to the creator of the service invention-creation, and their amounts do not comply with the provisions of Article 76 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law. On the other hand, the timing of these rewards was before Yiwei Company entered into the contract with Denso Corporation, and they are unrelated to the remuneration claimed by the plaintiff in this case. In summary, the aforementioned assertions made by the two defendants at trial are not supported.

**II. Concerning the Second Dispute Focus**

The two patents-in-suit were declared invalid on December 23, 2005. In the absence of evidence from Plaintiff Weng Like showing that the two patents are still in a valid legal status, the plaintiff can only demand that Defendant Yiwei Company pay the corresponding remuneration derived from the collection of patent license fees before the patents were declared invalid.

Regarding the calculation base: First, analyzing the relevant clauses of the "P7 and PE Type Diesel Injection Pump Technology Transfer Agreement," the consideration for the payments received by Defendant Yiwei Company under the agreement is "the provision of technical information pursuant to Section 3.1 of this Agreement and the licensed rights pursuant to Article 2 of this Agreement." However, the "technical information" listed in the appendix to the agreement does not entirely correspond directly to the technology of the contracted products, P7 pumps and PE pump assemblies. Based on the proportion determined by the supplementary appraisal conclusion issued by the Science and Technology Consulting Center, approximately 70% of the contract payments received by Yiwei Company constitutes the license fee related to the licensing of the fuel injection pump assembly technology. Second, because the patents-in-suit are only part of the fuel injection pump assembly technology, the fees related to the patents within the license fees for the fuel injection pump assembly technology should be further determined based on the technical contribution rate of the patents in the P7 pump or PE pump. According to the appraisal conclusion issued by the Science and Technology Consulting Center, approximately 5% of the license fee for the P7 pump assembly technology corresponds to the benefits derived from the patent "Locking Spring Device for the Roller of the Tappet of a Fuel Injection Pump" applied in that product. Approximately 10% of the license fee for the PE pump assembly technology corresponds to the benefits derived from the two patents-in-suit applied in that product. Third, the base for calculating remuneration should be after-tax income. The agreement between Yiwei Company and Denso Corporation also stipulates that taxes are to be paid by the licensor, Yiwei Company, on its own. The plaintiff's assertion regarding tax reduction or exemption lacks supporting evidence and is not accepted. In summary, the calculation base for the remuneration of the patents-in-suit should be 70% of the contract payments received by Yiwei Company after taxation, combined with the respective technical contribution rates of the patents in the contracted products. Therefore, the net after-tax profit obtained by Yiwei Company from licensing the "Locking Spring Device for the Roller of the Tappet of a Fuel Injection Pump" patent to Denso Corporation for use in P7 pumps is RMB 168,104.69. The net after-tax profit obtained from licensing the two patents-in-suit to Denso Corporation for use in PE pumps is RMB 753,433.86.

Regarding the extraction ratio: Article 76 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law only sets a minimum ratio. The "Several Opinions on Further Strengthening Intellectual Property Work in Shanghai" stipulates: "Enterprises should further increase incentives for patent inventors and consciously protect the rights and interests of patent inventors. After a patent holder transfers a patent or licenses others to implement it, it may extract no less than 30% from the after-tax income as remuneration for the inventor or creator." The "Notice on Several Supporting Policies for Implementing the 'Shanghai Medium and Long-term Science and Technology Development Plan Outline (2006-2020)'" stipulates: "Effectively protect the rights and interests of patent inventors or creators. After a patent owner transfers a patent or licenses others to implement it, it may extract no less than 30% of the after-tax income as remuneration for the inventor or creator. Where the patent owner is a university or research institute, the extractable ratio is no less than 50%. Alternatively, technology investment by the inventor or creator may be implemented by reference to the above ratios." The aforementioned provisions use guiding language such as "may" and cannot directly determine the extraction ratio. Therefore, calculating the amount of remuneration for the inventor or creator in this case requires a comprehensive analysis of the case circumstances. Shortly after Plaintiff Weng Like filed this lawsuit, Denso Corporation petitioned the Patent Reexamination Board to declare the patents-in-suit invalid. At trial, the plaintiff claimed that the evidence holder for the grounds relied upon by Denso Corporation should be the Defendants Shangchai Company and Yiwei Company, and that there is an apparent affiliated relationship between the two defendants. The sales facts between them are insufficient to negate the novelty of the patents. The plaintiff argued that Denso Corporation's petition to declare the patents-in-suit invalid was an illegal act of malicious collusion with the two defendants. The court holds that, as this is a civil lawsuit, this part of the matter will not be tried. However, considering Yiwei Company's passive behavior of failing to take effective measures to salvage the patent rights within three months after receiving the decision on the invalidity declaration request, the invalidation of the patents-in-suit directly prevented the plaintiff from claiming remuneration based on the economic benefits that would have arisen from the continued promotion and application of the patents-in-suit before their expiration. Considering all factors of the case comprehensively, the extraction ratio is determined to be 30%.

In summary, the amount payable by Defendant Yiwei Company is calculated as 30% of the net after-tax profit of RMB 168,104.69 from licensing the "Locking Spring Device for the Roller of the Tappet of a Fuel Injection Pump" patent to Denso Corporation for use in P7 pumps, which is RMB 50,431.41, plus 30% of the net after-tax profit of RMB 753,433.86 from licensing the two patents-in-suit to Denso Corporation for use in PE pumps, which is RMB 226,030.16. The sum of these two amounts is RMB 276,461.57.

Accordingly, on December 25, 2007, the Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court rendered the judgment:

1. Defendant Yiwei Company shall extract RMB 276,461.57 from the fees collected for licensing the implementation of the two utility model patents, Patent No. ZL01238898.X "Locking Spring Device for the Roller of the Tappet of a Fuel Injection Pump" and Patent No. ZL01238896.3 "Rectangular Cross-Section Plunger Spring Fuel Injection Pump," as remuneration payable to Plaintiff Weng Like; 2. The remainder of the plaintiff's claims is dismissed.

Court acceptance fee of RMB 20,010: Plaintiff Weng Like shall bear RMB 8,622; Defendant Yiwei Company shall bear RMB 11,388. Technical appraisal fee of RMB 52,000: Plaintiff shall bear RMB 12,000; Yiwei Company shall bear RMB 40,000.

Both Weng Like and Yiwei Company were dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment and appealed to the Shanghai High People's Court.

**Appellant Weng Like's** appeal request sought reversal of the original judgment and an order that Appellant Yiwei Company and Defendant at First Instance Shangchai Company pay him the service remuneration of RMB 2,000,000 for the license fees of the patents-in-suit. The main reasons were: First, the "Technical Appraisal Report" and the "Supplementary Appraisal Report" issued by the Science and Technology Consulting Center are completely unreliable and unreasonable. The first-instance judgment's findings on the technical contribution of the patents-in-suit, the "proportion of the fuel injection pump assembly technology" in the transfer fee, and the "calculation base" for the service remuneration are completely erroneous in fact. The "technical contribution rate composition" proposed in the "Technical Appraisal Report" was neither based on factual investigation nor subjected to necessary technical analysis. The conclusion in the "Supplementary Appraisal Report" that "the technical proportion of P7 pump and PE pump assembly technology in the total transferred content under the agreement is approximately 70%; the proportion of the management system is approximately 30%" lacks factual basis. The 30% "extraction ratio" is only applicable in general circumstances. Given the specific circumstances of this case, the extraction ratio could be further increased to 50% or even higher. Second, the first-instance judgment failed to ascertain whether the technology transfer fees (royalties) involved were subject to tax or exempt from tax, resulting in an erroneous calculation base, which is a finding of unclear facts. Third, the first-instance judgment's ruling that the claim for joint liability of Shangchai Company for paying service remuneration for the corresponding period "lacks legal basis" constitutes improper application of law. Before April 23, 2004, the patentee of "Rectangular Cross-Section Plunger Spring Fuel Injection Pump" was Shangchai Company; before February 7, 2004, the patentee of "Locking Spring Device for the Roller of the Tappet of a Fuel Injection Pump" was Shangchai Company. Shangchai Company should bear the corresponding legal liability for the service invention remuneration dispute during the corresponding period according to law. Fourth, the invalidation of the patents-in-suit was caused by the fault of Yiwei Company and Shangchai Company, resulting in loss of expected benefits. The "time period for calculating remuneration" should be extended to the expiration date of the patents-in-suit in April 2011.

**Appellant Yiwei Company's** appeal request sought reversal of the original judgment and a new judgment according to law. The main reasons were: First, the patents-in-suit have already been invalidated, so Yiwei Company should not pay the relevant remuneration. Second, the first-instance judgment's extraction of remuneration at 30% is unreasonable. Third, the first-instance judgment's apportionment of 80% of the appraisal fees to Yiwei Company is unreasonable; the fees should be shared according to the degree of liability.

**Appellant Weng Like's** reply argued that Appellant Yiwei Company's appeal request lacks legal basis: First, he agreed with the first-instance judgment's reasoning that although the patents-in-suit were declared invalid, Yiwei Company is still obligated to pay the service remuneration. Second, the extraction of patent license fees has a floor but no ceiling. Third, the fault in this case lies with Yiwei Company and Shangchai Company, so Yiwei Company should naturally bear most of the appraisal fees.

**Appellant Yiwei Company's** reply argued: First, the two appraisal reports are scientific and rigorous, and the appraisal conclusions are essentially accurate. Second, the invalidation of the patents-in-suit was not malicious, but the extraction of patent license fees at a 30% ratio is too high. Third, he fully agreed with the first-instance judgment's reasoning that Shangchai Company should not bear joint liability. Appellant Weng Like's appeal lacks legal basis and should be dismissed.

The Defendant at First Instance, Shangchai Company, did not appeal. It stated agreement with Appellant Yiwei Company's reply arguments and claimed that it was not in a tax-exempt situation.

**During the second instance**, none of the parties submitted new evidence.

**The Shanghai High People's Court**, upon trial, confirmed the facts found in the first instance.

**The Shanghai High People's Court held in the second instance:**

**I. Concerning Appellant Weng Like's Appeal Contentions.**

The first-instance court's entrustment of the Science and Technology Consulting Center to conduct the technical appraisal in question was procedurally lawful. The appraisal experts, after fully hearing the opinions of all parties, comprehensively reviewing the materials relevant to the appraisal submitted by all parties, and applying their professional knowledge and experience, reached appraisal conclusions that should be adopted. Appellant Weng Like's assertion that the "Technical Appraisal Report" and the "Supplementary Appraisal Report" are unreliable and unreasonable lacks sufficient factual and legal basis and is not supported. According to the provisions of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law, Appellant Yiwei Company's obligation is to extract no less than 10% from the after-tax license fees collected for licensing the implementation of the patents-in-suit as remuneration to be paid to Weng Like. The first-instance court, considering the actual circumstances of this case and making a comprehensive analysis, determined the patent license fee extraction ratio to be 30%. This complies with legal provisions, the reasoning is sound, and it should be affirmed. Weng Like's current request to increase the extraction ratio to 50% or even higher, without submitting new evidence or providing other sufficient reasons, is not supported.

According to the provisions of the Ministry of Finance and the State Administration of Taxation's "Notice on Several Preferential Tax Policies for Enterprise Income Tax" (Cai Shui [1994] No. 001), the income of enterprises and institutions from technology transfer, as well as technology consulting, technical services, and technical training related to the technology transfer process, with an annual net income of RMB 300,000 or less, is temporarily exempted from enterprise income tax. However, the prerequisite is the approval of the tax authorities. According to the provisions of the Ministry of Finance and the State Administration of Taxation's "Notice on Issues Concerning the Implementation of Tax Policies Related to the 'Decision of the CPC Central Committee and the State Council on Strengthening Technological Innovation, Developing High Technology, and Realizing Industrialization'" (Cai Shui Zi [1999] No. 273), business tax is exempted on income derived by units and individuals (including foreign-invested enterprises, research and development centers established by foreign investment, foreign enterprises, and foreign individuals) from engaging in technology transfer, technology development business, and related technology consulting and technical services. However, the tax exemption must go through an approval procedure: When a taxpayer engaged in technology transfer or development business applies for business tax exemption, it must submit the written contract for technology transfer or development to the provincial-level science and technology competent authority where the taxpayer is located for certification. Then, it must submit the relevant written contract and the certification opinion of the science and technology competent authority to the local provincial-level competent tax authority for review. In summary, handling tax exemption matters requires undergoing corresponding review procedures. Appellant Weng Like failed to provide evidence related to such review in either the first or second instance. He merely argued that the status of taxation or tax exemption had not been clarified. However, relying solely on this suspicion as grounds for demanding an increase in the amount of patent use fee extraction lacks factual basis and is not supported.

Regarding Appellant Weng Like's request that the Defendant at First Instance, Shangchai Company, should bear joint liability with Appellant Yiwei Company, the first-instance court provided sufficient reasoning and accurately stated the law on this point. This reasoning should be affirmed. Therefore, Weng Like's claim for joint liability between Shangchai Company and Yiwei Company is not supported.

Regarding Appellant Weng Like's request for a share of the expected future profits, extending the "time period for calculating remuneration" to the expiration date of the patents-in-suit in April 2011: According to the Patent Law and its Implementing Regulations, the share of patent license fees as remuneration for the inventor or creator is a share of the benefits already realized from the exploitation of the corresponding patent. It does not include a share of expected future benefits. Therefore, Weng Like's claim on this point lacks legal basis and is not supported. Weng Like argued that the invalidation of the patents-in-suit was attributable to Appellant Yiwei Company. However, as this is a civil lawsuit, this issue is not within the scope of trial in this case. Weng Like may seek a separate resolution.

**II. Concerning Appellant Yiwei Company's Appeal Contentions.**

The first-instance judgment ordered Appellant Yiwei Company to pay Appellant Weng Like a share of the patent license fees. This was a share of the patent license fees accrued before the patents-in-suit were declared invalid. These fees were already realized by Yiwei Company from licensing the patents-in-suit. There is no situation here where the patentee Yiwei Company maliciously caused losses to the licensee Denso Corporation. According to the provisions of the Patent Law, Yiwei Company is under no obligation to refund the patent license fees already collected from the licensee Denso Corporation before the patents-in-suit were declared invalid. Yiwei Company's appeal argument that, because the patents-in-suit are already invalid, it should not pay the relevant remuneration, cannot stand.

Appellant Yiwei Company further appealed that the first-instance judgment's allocation of 80% of the appraisal fees to Yiwei Company was improper. The court holds that the first-instance court, based on the specific circumstances of this case, appropriately adjusted the patent use fee sharing ratio and allocated the appraisal fees at its discretion, which complies with legal provisions. Yiwei Company's ground of appeal on this point is not established and is not supported.

In summary, the appeal requests of both Appellant Weng Like and Appellant Yiwei Company lack factual and legal basis and should be dismissed. Accordingly, on April 18, 2008, the Shanghai High People's Court, pursuant to subparagraph (1) of paragraph 1 of Article 153 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the judgment:

**Appeal dismissed; judgment affirmed.**

The second-instance court acceptance fee for this case is RMB 5,446, to be borne equally by Appellant Weng Like and Appellant Yiwei Company, each paying RMB 2,723.

**This judgment is final.**
